rationale: Interpreted the isolation receipt and closed the containment question. Receipt d2973ec8cc524a9089c63dd046e1a4ff evaluated all four comparisons as declared: the feature-enabled node, whose configuration is empty, was isolated for a second and never campaigned (configured_servers 0, campaigning_observed false), while the control holding {A,B,C} became a candidate (configured_servers 3, campaigning_observed true). Both kept their term, which the operands show; that is the pre-vote extension rather than a failure to campaign, so the term stays an operand. The child account was rewritten so the refusal to campaign is an executed observation rather than a source-derived one, leaving only the vote-granting behaviour with an empty configuration as source-derived.

interpretations.rationale: This experiment characterises containment rather than a defect, and its predicates are all satisfied. Admission index 0 records the fixture (no snapshots on A, ten committed commands, A reporting {A,B,C} while running). After the feature-enabled restart, isolating the node from every peer for one second - twenty heartbeat timeouts at the configured 50ms - left it a follower that never entered candidate or leader state, with zero configured servers (comparisons 0 and 1 hold at index 2). The control restart, holding three configured servers, became a candidate during the same isolation (comparisons 2 and 3 hold at index 4), so the isolation is a real trigger and the empty configuration is what keeps the feature-enabled node from campaigning. Both nodes kept their term across the window (3 to 3, operands at indices 2 and 4), which the pre-vote extension explains: a candidate runs a pre-vote before incrementing its term, so the control could be observed in candidate state without a term change. Limits: the observation is a 1-second sample every 5ms in one run per mode, no votes were solicited from real peers, and the fault injected is transport disconnection only.
counterevidence: The control's candidate state shows the isolation would produce campaigning if a configuration were present, so the feature-enabled node's silence is attributable to the empty configuration.
The unchanged terms in both modes show the term operand must not be read as evidence of campaigning either way, given pre-vote.
limitations: One second of sampling per mode, no repetition across schedules.
No votes are solicited, so no election outcome is executed for either mode.
Transport disconnection is the only fault; no crash or store failure is involved.

interpretations.rationale: Answer: a node restarted with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs while it has no snapshot comes up with an empty configuration, and the election gate keeps that from turning into a stray candidate. Receipt bdf2837a4c004f95b6c9b19db4fb8154 records the restarts: the feature-enabled node reports no servers at all although its FSM replayed to index 13, while the same restart without the feature reports {A,B,C}; the mechanism is the scan starting at max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1 with lastApplied already raised to the persisted commit index, so with no snapshot no configuration entry is processed. Receipt d2973ec8cc524a9089c63dd046e1a4ff then isolates each restarted node for a second: the empty-configuration node never campaigns, while the control holding {A,B,C} becomes a candidate, which is the guard at raft.go 225-246 refusing to start an election while latestIndex is zero. What remains source-derived is only the vote side: a node with an empty configuration skips the membership check in requestVote (raft.go 1660-1680) and would grant votes to candidates it cannot evaluate. Remaining limits: the empty configuration is observed at construction with a 300ms settle; the absence of snapshots is arranged by the harness rather than caused by a store failure; the isolation is transport-only and lasts one second; and in-memory stores with scaled timeouts were used.
counterevidence: The control restart with the same stores and procedure rebuilds {A,B,C}, so the empty configuration is not a property of the stores or the restart.
The node's FSM replayed the log to index 13, so missing entries do not explain the empty configuration.
The control campaigned under the same isolation while the empty-configuration node did not, which supports the guard rather than a harness artefact.
limitations: The empty configuration is observed at construction; the isolation is a 1-second transport-only window with no vote solicitation.
The absence of snapshots is arranged by the harness (ten-minute interval, none taken) rather than caused by a store failure.
Vote granting with an empty configuration remains source-derived, not executed.
In-memory stores, scaled timeouts and a graceful shutdown; one run per mode.
interpretations.joint_history: Two receipts of two fixed experiments on one question: bdf2837a4c004f95b6c9b19db4fb8154 records the restarts and the configuration each produces, and d2973ec8cc524a9089c63dd046e1a4ff is the revision of the same harness that adds the isolation phase and records whether the restarted node campaigns. They are compatible because both observe the same cluster identity, the same restart procedure (same stores, same leader B, ten committed commands, no snapshot on A) and the same two resulting configurations (empty for the feature-enabled restart, {A,B,C} for the control); each comparison outcome is read from its own receipt.
